title: Utility company reminds homeowners to be safe
text:
Rhode Island Energy is encouraging homeowners to remain vigilant as the Ocean State continues to face the coldest stretch of weather in nearly a decade.
Snow and ice around gas meters, regulators and appliance vents can create hazardous conditions and disrupt the safe operation of the equipment. Ice, icicles and heavy snow falling from roofs can also cause damage.
The utility company is asking its customers to regularly inspect their equipment and “be mindful” when maintaining it.
Blocked exhaust or air-intake vents can cause carbon monoxide to build up indoors. The vents should be free of snow and ice to ensure detectors are working properly.
Meters and pressure regulators also have small vents that must stay unobstructed.
The company says when removing the blockages, people should use their hands or a broom to gently clear snow and ice from meters, regulators and exposed piping. Shovels can easily cause damage to equipment.
